questions.q: What does Pressfield call the inner force that makes you procrastinate?
a: Resistance
Inertia
Avoidance
Friction
questions.why: The overview describes Resistance as the force that lets you put off the work that matters most to you.

questions.q: What does Henry Fonda's example show about fear and important work?
a: Even masters never stop feeling afraid
Fear fades once you are famous
Rituals are needed before any performance
Acting is more stressful than other work
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Fonda threw up before every show even at seventy-five, because caring about your work keeps the fear alive.

questions.q: How does the summary define courage?
a: Moving forward even when you feel afraid
Never feeling fear before a challenge
Taking risks without any preparation
Ignoring what other people think
questions.why: Lesson 1 says acting in spite of fear is precisely what courage means.

questions.q: Why is it a bad idea to edit your work right after finishing it?
a: You are too close to it to judge it fairly
You will forget what you originally meant
The first draft is usually the strongest
Editing too soon damages your motivation
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends putting temporal and physical distance between creating and judging your work.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest doing when you feel like giving up?
a: Review what you have already accomplished
Take a long break from the project
Ask a friend to hold you accountable
Set a smaller goal for the day
questions.why: Lesson 3 says looking at your past progress renews your drive, then ask how badly and why you want it.
